Orderings of a Multiset, Counted With Multiplicity

Source: R/sum_struct.R
multiset_orderings.Rd

All \(n!\) orderings of a vector of indices, without deduplicating the ones that coincide because an index repeats: multiset_orderings(c(1, 1)) returns two elements.

Usage

multiset_orderings(v)

Arguments

v

An integer vector, of length 0 to 3 in every call the package makes, the expansion at order \(n\) permuting the \(n-1\) indices after the first.

Value

A list of factorial(length(v)) integer vectors.

Details

The distinction is load bearing, and its cost is measured. The cyclic sum behind the log-determinant expansion runs over \((n-1)!\) orderings, and two that happen to be equal still count twice; deduplicating them leaves a third derivative in one weight too small by exactly 2 and a fourth by exactly 6, which is \(2!\) and \(3!\), the orderings of the tail. Both are numbers a reader would accept without noticing.

See also

sum_struct_trace_term(), the only caller, and combinat_perms(), which does the same for the matrix logarithm's contraction.
